children: 0830 JST (2330 GMT/1830 EST Thursday, November 26) The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications releases November Tokyo CPI.

Mace News median: total CPI +3.0% y/y (range: +3.0% to +3.3%) vs. Oct +2.8%; core CPI (ex-fresh food) +2.9% (range: +2.8% to +3.1%) vs. Oct +2.6%; core-core CPI (ex-fresh food, energy) +2.8% (range: +2.7% to +2.9%) vs. Oct +2.6%

TOKYO (MaceNews) - Consumer inflation in Tokyo, a leading indicator of the national trend, is expected to accelerate in all three key readings in November as electricity charges surged after the government ended its summer subsidies at the end of September, having clearer influence on pushing up overall consumer prices.

International oil prices remained elevated amid the unsettled situation in the Middle East. Coupled with the yen’s weakness, higher energy costs were spreading more widely, including through Japanese electricity bills, adding to broad inflationary pressure. Other raw material prices also remained elevated, with import prices staying high amid the weak Japanese currency.
These factors appear to have boosted the core Tokyo consumer price index (CPI), which excludes fresh food, to a 16-month high of 2.9% in November, up from 2.6% in October.

Consumer inflation has started to trend upward as the Tokyo metropolitan government and the central government began scaling back subsidies in recent months. Without fiscal support programs for households, upward price pressures are expected to remain in place.

In addition, there are few signs that this trend will ease, with higher energy, import and labor costs forcing firms in many sectors to raise prices. The conflict in the Middle East continues, while the yen remains weaker than a year earlier, eroding Japan’s purchasing power.

The two other key readings are also expected to accelerate in November, with the total CPI seen reaching 3.0%, its highest level since June 2025, when it stood 3.1%, after rising 2.8% in October. The core-core index, which excludes both fresh food and energy, is expected to rise 2.8% in November, compared with 2.6% a month earlier.

title: Japan Data Preview: Tokyo CPI Expected Up to 16-Month High in November
